record.original_question: How can one define the most plausible initial conditions at the beginning of the hydrodynamic stage in a relativistic heavy-ion collision? The issue is to specify the initial relativistic-fluid state at the start of stage (ii), even though the experimentally observed hadrons are produced only much later and the earlier state cannot be measured directly.

evidence.quote: Question 4.2. How can we define the most plausible initial conditions at the beginning of step (ii)?
The problem linked to initial conditions is that this is very unclear how to specify these conditions in the experimental context described here.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the standard multi-stage description of an ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collision, the evolution of the produced matter is commonly split into: (i) a pre-equilibrium stage immediately after the collision, in which strongly out-of-equilibrium gluon/parton dynamics dominate; (ii) a relativistic hydrodynamic stage, modeled by the equations of relativistic (viscous) fluid dynamics for an energy-momentum tensor T^{μν}(x) with prescribed equation of state and transport coefficients; (iii) a hadronization / freeze-out stage, after which the resulting hadrons stream freely and are eventually detected.

The hydrodynamic stage (ii) is an initial-value problem: given a space-like (or proper-time) hypersurface Σ_0 at the start of stage (ii), one must specify on Σ_0 the full set of fluid fields—energy density ε(x), flow four-velocity u^μ(x) (with u^μ u_μ = −1), and the dissipative components (e.g. shear-stress tensor π^{μν}, bulk pressure Π, baryon diffusion)—as initial data for the relativistic hydrodynamic evolution equations.

The fundamental difficulty is that the state on Σ_0 cannot be measured directly: only the asymptotic hadrons produced after stage (iii) are experimentally observed, while the matter on Σ_0 is hidden behind subsequent non-trivial dynamics.

Problem. Provide a principled mathematical/physical prescription that determines, from first principles or from a controlled effective description of the pre-equilibrium dynamics in stage (i), the most plausible initial data (ε, u^μ, π^{μν}, Π, …) on the initial hypersurface Σ_0 of the hydrodynamic stage in a relativistic heavy-ion collision, in such a way that the prescription is:

(a) compatible with the underlying microscopic theory (QCD) governing stage (i);
(b) capable of producing initial conditions whose subsequent hydrodynamic evolution and freeze-out yield predictions consistent with the experimentally observed hadronic final state;
(c) able to characterize the event-by-event fluctuations of these initial conditions.

In particular, formulate and justify a definition of "the most plausible initial conditions" at the onset of the hydrodynamic stage.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews on relativistic hydrodynamics in heavy-ion collisions explicitly state that the specification of thermal initial conditions on the hydrodynamic hypersurface remains an open problem: it depends on a pre-equilibrium / thermalization dynamics that is not fully understood, and several competing initial-condition models (Glauber, KLN, IP-Glasma, EKRT, dynamical initialization, etc.) are still in use without a first-principles consensus.

status_evidence.title: Relativistic hydrodynamics in heavy-ion collisions: general aspects and recent developments
status_evidence.snippet: The precise knowledge of the preequilibrium stage is essential input in viscous hydrodynamics models, and the knowledge of distribution of energy/entropy density and the thermalization time is one of the uncertainties present in current hydrodynamics model studies.
status_evidence.claim: Specification of initial conditions for the hydrodynamic stage remains an unresolved input/uncertainty.

status_evidence.title: Dynamical initialization and hydrodynamic modeling of relativistic heavy-ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Thermal initial conditions are a consequence of prethermal dynamics which is not completely understood yet.
status_evidence.claim: Initial conditions are derived from prethermal dynamics that is still not completely understood.

status_evidence.title: Initial state and flow physics — A theoretical overview
status_evidence.snippet: Understanding initial conditions of the relativistic heavy ion collisions is a necessary condition for understanding the rest of the later phenomena.
status_evidence.claim: Determining the initial state is recognized as an outstanding theoretical problem.
